Comparison

Suno vs Udio

A side-by-side look at Suno and Udio, using the details in each tool profile.

Quick take

Choose Suno when your priority is: complete songs with vocals generated from a text description. Choose Udio when your priority is: higher-fidelity generated music with section-by-section control.

Suno vs Udio at a glance

CriteriaSunoUdio
CategoryAI Audio & Music ToolsAI Audio & Music Tools
Best forComplete songs with vocals generated from a text description.Higher-fidelity generated music with section-by-section control.
Pricing modelFreemiumFreemium
Free planYesYes
Free trialNoNo
API availableNot verifiedNo
Platforms
  • Web, iOS, Android
  • Discord
  • Web, iOS, Android
Key features
  • Full song generation with vocals from a text prompt
  • custom lyrics input or AI lyric writing
  • genre, mood and style prompting
  • Personas for consistent artist voice across tracks
  • Covers reinterpreting an existing track in a new style
  • Extend and Remaster
  • High-fidelity song generation with vocals
  • iterative Extend workflow building a track section by section
  • inpainting to regenerate a specific portion of a track
  • audio upload and remix
  • manual mode for detailed control over structure
  • stem separation
Advantages
  • Vocal quality and song coherence are the best available - complete, structured, listenable songs from a prompt is genuinely impressive
  • very cheap for the output volume
  • commercial rights included at $10/mo
  • Personas give consistency across a project.
  • Audio fidelity and production polish are generally judged a step above Suno by musicians
  • the inpainting feature - regenerating just one section - gives control nothing else in this pair offers
  • manual mode allows genuine structural direction
  • stem export enables real DAW work.
Limitations
  • limited fine-grained control over arrangement compared with a DAW
  • no MIDI export
  • output can sound generic and recognisably AI-generated
  • stem separation quality varies
  • the short-generation-plus-extend workflow consumes more credits and takes longer than Suno's one-shot approach
  • smaller user base and community
  • no API
  • free tier is more restrictive than Suno's daily refresh.

Pricing notes

Suno

Free/Basic $0 with roughly 50 credits per day (about 10 songs), non-commercial use only. Pro around $10/mo ($8 annually) with roughly 2,500 credits/month (about 500 songs), commercial use rights and 10 concurrent generations. Premier around $30/mo ($24 annually) with roughly 10,000 credits/month (about 2,000 songs) and priority. Enterprise available. Annual billing roughly 20% cheaper.

Udio

Free with roughly 100 credits per month (plus some daily allowance historically), non-commercial. Standard around $10/mo ($8 annually) with roughly 1,200 credits/month and commercial rights. Pro around $30/mo ($24 annually) with roughly 4,800 credits/month, priority generation and stem downloads. Annual billing roughly 20% cheaper. Verify - Udio has adjusted credit allowances several times.

Prices change often. Confirm on the official pricing pages: Suno ↗ · Udio ↗

Frequently asked questions

What is the main difference between Suno and Udio?

Suno: Text-to-music generator producing complete songs with vocals, lyrics, instrumentation and structure from a prompt. Udio: Text-to-music generator competing directly with Suno, generally rated slightly higher on audio fidelity and production quality while offering somewhat shorter initial generations that are extended iteratively.

When should I choose Suno over Udio?

Suno is listed as best for: complete songs with vocals generated from a text description. Udio is listed as best for: higher-fidelity generated music with section-by-section control.

Do Suno and Udio have a free plan?

Suno: Yes. Udio: Yes. Check each official pricing page, as plans change.
